disposition_reason: Narrative review of Cd exposure and toxicity in honey bees (bee bodies, larvae, molecular responses). Honey is mentioned only as one of the bee products in the Introduction; no honey Cd data or honey survey synthesis, so it supplies bee-exposure and apiary-siting context only.
disposition_locator: Introduction (md line 19); 'Cd Exposure of Bees' (md lines 53-67); Conclusion (md line 127)

study.material_scope: honey bees (adult and larval), pollen and nectar as exposure route; honey not a reviewed matrix

controls.control: Apiary location relative to industrial zones and mining
controls.comparator: industrial vs urban vs rural; mining vs non-mining
controls.outcome: Bees near industrial zones in Serbia had significantly higher Cd than urban or rural bees; bees near a Sardinian mining area more affected; Cd greater in urban than rural areas in Italy, Poland and Turkey.
controls.locator: section 'Cd Exposure of Bees', md copy lines 61 (approx. article PDF p.3 from _page_N_ image markers)
controls.note: Measured matrix is bee bodies, not honey.

controls.control: Rural/agricultural siting is not by itself protective for Cd
controls.outcome: Substantial Cd reported in bees from agricultural zones and seemingly unpolluted rural areas, in some cases higher than industrial zones; Cd pollution is ubiquitous.
controls.locator: section 'Abstract; Cd Exposure of Bees', md copy lines 13, 61 (approx. article PDF p.3 from _page_N_ image markers)
controls.note: Important qualifier for any 'site away from industry' control: bee-body data, not honey.

controls.control: Forage plant species determine Cd exposure; bees do not avoid contaminated forage
controls.outcome: Plants (pollen and nectar) are the primary Cd exposure route; bees cannot discriminate metal-contaminated from clean plants; Cd varies between plant species, cultivars and genotypes; dose-dependent relation between feed Cd and bee Cd.
controls.locator: section 'Cd Exposure of Bees', md copy lines 55, 59 (approx. article PDF p.3 from _page_N_ image markers)
controls.note: Review notes that nectar Cd data are especially limited.

controls.control: Airborne deposition and seasonal timing of exposure
controls.outcome: Airborne Cd deposition substantially higher in winter, especially near industrial areas; non-essential elements in bees higher in spring/summer when bees are most active; significant variation over 3 months at one location (van der Steen) attributed to anthropogenic emission fluctuations.
controls.locator: section 'Cd Exposure of Bees', md copy lines 63-65, 127 (approx. article PDF p.3 from _page_N_ image markers)
controls.note: Bee-body monitoring timing; no harvest-timing recommendation for honey is made.

controls.control: Anthropogenic Cd sources to avoid near apiaries
controls.outcome: Mining, smelting/refining, fossil fuel combustion, cement production, phosphate fertilisers, municipal/sewage sludge incineration, landfill leaching of batteries/electronics/solar panels, PVC stabilisers and pigments.
controls.locator: section 'Cadmium (Cd)', md copy lines 49 (approx. article PDF p.2 from _page_N_ image markers)

controls.control: Honey bees and bee products as Cd bioindicators
controls.outcome: Potential role of honey bees and their products as bioindicators for toxic metal pollution highlighted.
controls.locator: section 'Introduction', md copy lines 35 (approx. article PDF p.1 from _page_N_ image markers)

notes: Studies cited that measure honey itself and could be traced for occurrence (titles in reference list): [47] Formicki et al. 2013 (metal content in honey, propolis, wax, bee pollen); [53] Bayir & Aygun 2022 (honey bees, honey and pollen, rural vs urban Konya); [54] Scivicco et al. 2022 (dietary exposure to heavy metals through polyfloral honey, Campania); [62] Ciric et al. 2021 (honey bees and their products as indicators); [61] Gutierrez et al. 2020 (nectar). Bee-toxicity numbers verified in source: Cronn LD50 CdCl2 3.51/2.80 ug Cd/bee (48/96 h), CdSO4 2.34/1.44 ug Cd/bee; Di et al. forager LC50 78 mg/L; larval LC50 0.275 mg/L; growth reduction from 1.05 mg/L; 100% mortality 9.47-28.41 mg/L (md lines 77-79).
contradictions_with_stored_summary: Summary states the review traces Cd 'carryover into honey' and that it synthesises '(3) honey and pollen Cd residue surveys'; the review body contains no honey Cd data and no honey survey synthesis; 'honey' occurs only as a bee product in the Introduction (md line 19) and in reference titles.
Summary frontmatter lists matrices [honey, bee-pollen, bee-body-tissue]; honey is not a reviewed matrix.
Summary's certification implication ('supports Cd as the primary analyte to track when honey ... appear[s] in food formulations') is not stated by the source.
Numeric statements in the summary (soil Cd 0.07-1.1 mg/kg, 1300-41000 t/yr natural emission, 25-30 yr half-life, LD50/LC50 values) match the source.
